q: 为什么内存缓存通常比数据库读得快？
q_en: Why is an in-memory cache usually faster than database reads?
options: Redis 索引一定比数据库索引高级
内存路径避开磁盘访问延迟
C 语言实现天然比 SQL 更快
数据库只慢在 SQL 解析阶段
why: 决定性约束是存储介质：内存离 CPU 近，通常避开磁盘寻道和页读取。经验法则是先用缓存加速高频读，但同时准备失效和降级。
why_en: A cache is faster mainly because memory is close to the CPU and avoids disk access, not because Redis has magic query logic.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    App["App"] --> Redis["Redis memory ~1ms"]
    App --> DB["Database disk ~50ms"]
scenario: 一次资料页读取要么查 Postgres，要么查 Redis；面试官在问为什么缓存读延迟能低一个数量级。
scenario_en: A profile-page read can hit Postgres or Redis; the interviewer is asking why cache read latency can be an order of magnitude lower.
options_en: Redis indexes are always more advanced than database indexes.
The memory path avoids disk-access latency.
C implementations are naturally faster than SQL.
Databases are slow only because of SQL parsing.

换成 C 写的磁盘库照样慢，语言不是主成本。

A C-based disk store is still slow, so language isn't the main cost.
Parsing is a tiny slice; disk I/O is the real cost.

why_en: For a multi-server app, start with an external shared cache because every server can read the same hot data while accepting cache-invalidation complexity.

q: 哪层缓存最直接？

options: CDN 边缘节点缓存媒体
Redis 缓存每个视频字节
应用进程内缓存全球媒体

optionExplanations: 对：瓶颈是跨洲距离时，CDN 把媒体放到就近边缘。
Redis 适合小动态 key，不缓存整段视频字节。
进程内只帮单机热点，覆盖不了全球用户。
查询缓存复用结果，但源站距离还在。

q: 这时最适合哪种缓存？
q_en: Which cache fits this case best?
options: 数据库加索引后每次查库
CDN 缓存配置接口
应用进程内缓存小配置
每次请求都查 Redis
why: 后端每请求都读很小的内部配置时，进程内直接读本机内存、连 Redis 跳都省；CDN 给用户拿公开内容，不管内部 flag。

options_en: Add a database index and query every time.
Cache the config API in a CDN.
Cache small config values in process.
Query Redis on every request.

q: 进程内缓存哪些判断成立？
q_en: Which statements about in-process caching are true?
options: 读取通常比 Redis 更快
每个应用实例各存一份
适合小而少变的热数据
失效会自动同步到所有实例
why: 进程内缓存省掉网络调用，所以读最快；但每个实例独立，失效不会自动广播。它是小而稳定热点数据的优化层，不是 Redis 替代品。
why_en: In-process cache is fastest because there is no network call, but each instance owns its copy and invalidation does not automatically propagate.
scenario: 评估是否把小配置、feature flag 和少量热点 key 放到应用进程内，而不是每次请求 Redis。
scenario_en: You are deciding whether tiny config, feature flags, and a few hot keys should live in process instead of calling Redis on every request.
options_en: Reads are usually faster than Redis.
Each application instance keeps its own copy.
It fits small, rarely-changing hot data.
Invalidation automatically syncs to all instances.

termDefinitions.meaning: 主动删除或过期缓存条目，让后续读取重新拿新值。

termDefinitions.meaning: 被高频访问的缓存 key，可能成为局部瓶颈。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hot key is a cache key that receives unusually high traffic and may become a bottleneck.

optionExplanations: 对：本地内存读没有网络跳，通常比 Redis 更快。
对：缓存副本属于各自进程，扩容后新实例各存一份。
对：小、稳定、少变的数据陈旧风险可控，适合放进程内。
错：本地缓存不会自动广播失效，要另建通道才同步。
optionExplanations_en: True: local memory reads have no network hop, so they're usually faster than Redis.
True: the cached copy belongs to each process, so new instances each keep their own.
True: small, stable, rarely-changing data has manageable staleness and fits in-process.
False: local caches don't auto-broadcast invalidation; you'd need a separate channel.

q: 两者在共享性上怎么不同？
q_en: How do Redis and in-process cache differ on sharing?
options: 两者都天然跨服务器共享
进程内共享，Redis 不共享
Redis 共享，进程内不共享
两者都只能单机内使用

why_en: Redis is shared because it is an external service, while in-process cache is per instance and trades sharing for local speed.
scenario: 同一个热点配置被 20 台应用服务器读取；你要比较本地进程内缓存和外部 Redis 的共享能力。
scenario_en: The same hot config is read by 20 app servers; compare local in-process cache with external Redis on sharing.
options_en: Both are naturally shared across servers.
In-process is shared, while Redis is not.
Redis is shared, while in-process is not.
Both can only be used on one machine.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: A shared cache is one cache service accessed by multiple application servers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存里的旧值和数据库里的新值不一致。

Backwards: in-process is a per-instance copy; Redis is the shared one.
Right: Redis is a standalone service shared by many servers; in-process is per-instance.
Wrong: Redis exists precisely for cross-server sharing, not single-machine use.

q: 这个量级最支持哪条设计判断？

缓存会让写入天然强一致
一次性验证码也应长期缓存
schema 设计好就不需要缓存

Caching makes writes strongly consistent by default.

A good schema means caching is never needed.

q: 补全四种核心缓存读写模式：
q_en: Fill in the four core cache read/write patterns:
text: 四种缓存架构：{{Cache-Aside}}（旁路 / 懒加载）、{{Write-Through}}（写穿透）、{{Write-Behind}}（写回 / write-back）、{{Read-Through}}（读穿透）。
why: 这四个名字分属两条轴：Cache-Aside/Read-Through 定义读 miss 谁查 DB；Write-Through/Write-Behind 定义写请求怎么落库。写策略本身不说明读怎么做，读侧要另选。
why_en: These names sit on two axes: cache-aside/read-through define who handles read misses, while write-through/write-behind define how writes reach the DB.

rows: 先写 Cache 后刷 DB

whenOtherWins: 默认读多降 DB 压力选 Cache-Aside；想把回源逻辑封装在缓存层选 Read-Through；读必须尽量新鲜选 Write-Through；写入峰值大且可接受最终一致/少量丢失风险选 Write-Behind。

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用先查缓存；未命中时应用查数据库并回填缓存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: In cache-aside, the app checks cache first and fills it after a database read on a miss.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写入必须同步更新缓存和数据库后才算完成；它不单独定义读 miss 怎么处理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write-through completes a write only after both cache and database are updated.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先写缓存，再由后台异步批量写数据库；它不单独定义读 miss 怎么处理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write-behind writes cache first and flushes changes to the database asynchronously.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存未命中时由缓存层自己去数据库取数并回填。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Read-through lets the cache fetch from the database and fill itself on a miss.

termDefinitions.meaning: 读侧策略管 cache miss；写侧策略管写请求。两者可以组合，不是四选一。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Read-side policy handles cache misses; write-side policy handles writes. They can be combined.

diagram:
flowchart LR
    Read["Read policy"] --> CA["Cache-Aside: App fills miss"]
    Read --> RT["Read-Through: Cache fills miss"]
    Write["Write policy"] --> WT["Write-Through: sync DB"]
    Write --> WB["Write-Behind: async DB"]

scenario: 面试里只说系统读多、想降低数据库压力；没有强一致写入、极高写吞吐或 CDN 这类特殊要求。
scenario_en: In an interview, the only stated need is a read-heavy system that should reduce database load; there is no special consistency, write-throughput, or CDN requirement.
q: 默认用哪种缓存模式？
q_en: Which caching pattern is the default?
options: Write-Behind 异步写回
Cache-Aside 读时懒加载
Read-Through 缓存代理
Write-Through 同步双写
why: 无强一致/高写吞吐要求时默认 Cache-Aside：读 cache、miss 查库回填；简单但 miss 慢、可能陈旧。
why_en: Without special consistency or write-throughput needs, cache-aside is the default: read cache first, and on a miss the app reads DB and fills cache.
whenOtherWins: 写后必须立刻读到最新时，改用 Write-Through。
options_en: Use write-behind asynchronous flushes.
Use cache-aside lazy loading on reads.
Use a read-through cache proxy.
Use write-through synchronous double writes.
tradeoff: 简单可降级 vs miss/陈旧

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存里没有目标数据，请求必须去后端数据源获取。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cache miss means the value is absent from cache and must be fetched from the backing store.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只有数据真的被请求时才加载并缓存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Lazy loading stores data only when it is actually requested.

termDefinitions.meaning: 某个依赖故障时系统还能不能继续服务；它不等于数据一定不丢，也不等于一定最新。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Availability means whether the system can keep serving when a dependency fails; it is separate from durability and freshness.

optionExplanations: Write-Behind 优化写吞吐、可能丢，不是通用默认。
对：无特殊一致/吞吐要求时，Cache-Aside 最简单。
Read-Through 把回源下沉缓存层，适合 CDN/代理。
Write-Through 同步双写读更新鲜，但写更慢。
optionExplanations_en: Write-behind optimizes throughput and may lose data, not a general default.
Right: with no special consistency/throughput need, cache-aside is simplest.
Read-through pushes origin fetch into the cache, fitting CDN/proxy.
Write-through's sync double write keeps reads fresh but writes slower.

q: 补全 Cache-Aside 读取流程：
q_en: Fill in the cache-aside read flow:
text: 先查{{缓存}}；命中则直接返回；未命中则查{{数据库}}，把结果写回{{缓存}}，再返回。
why: Cache-Aside 的核心是「懒加载」：只有被读到的数据才进缓存。代价是第一次未命中会多一次数据库延迟。
why_en: Cache-aside checks the cache first, and on a miss reads the database, writes the result back to the cache, and returns it.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    App["App"] --> Cache{"Hit?"}
    Cache -->|yes| Return["Return"]
    Cache -->|no| DB["Read DB"]
    DB --> Set["Set TTL"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 先写缓存，后台异步批量落库，写吞吐最高但崩溃可能丢未刷数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write-behind writes to cache first and flushes to the DB asynchronously, maximizing write throughput at the risk of crash loss.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写请求同步更新缓存和数据库，两边都成功才算完成。

q: Write-Behind（写回）最大的风险是？

Write latency is extremely high because each write waits on the DB.
Reads always return a stale value.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先写缓存，后台异步批量落库；崩溃时未刷入库的那批会丢。

termDefinitions.meaning: 把缓存里累积的写批量提交到持久数据库。

termDefinitions.meaning: 写请求同步更新缓存和数据库，写慢但一写就持久。

termDefinitions.meaning: 写只落缓存、异步批量刷库，写快但崩溃可能丢。

q: 补全常见淘汰策略：
q_en: Fill in the common cache eviction policies:
text: {{LRU}} 淘汰最久未被访问的；{{LFU}} 淘汰访问次数最少的；{{FIFO}} 按插入顺序淘汰最老的；{{TTL}} 不是淘汰策略本身，而是给 key 设过期时间。

scenario: 面试里被问缓存淘汰策略，工作负载普通、没有特别的访问模式。

why_en: LRU is the safe default because recently used data tends to be used again, and it fits most workloads with constant-time eviction.
options_en: LRU (least recently used).
FIFO (first in, first out, by insertion order).
Random eviction.
Never evict.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全称 Least Recently Used：优先淘汰最久没被访问过的 key。

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存内存不够时选择删除哪些 key 来腾空间。

why: LFU 按访问频次淘汰，能长期保留「持续热门」的 key（每个 key 一个计数器；有的用近似 LFU 降成本），适合趋势/榜单类数据。
why_en: LFU evicts the least frequently accessed key, so it keeps consistently popular items like trending videos or top playlists.
options_en: FIFO.
TTL on its own, without any eviction policy.
LFU (least frequently used).
Random eviction.
tradeoff: 长期高频保留（LFU） vs 近期热点适配（LRU）
whenOtherWins: 热点只是‘最近’热、会随时间漂移时，LRU 更贴合。

termDefinitions.meaning: 全称 Least Frequently Used：优先淘汰访问次数最少的 key，留住长期高频项。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LFU (Least Frequently Used) evicts the least-accessed key, keeping persistently popular items.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全称 First In First Out：按插入顺序淘汰最早进来的 key。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FIFO (First In First Out) evicts the earliest-inserted key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全称 Time To Live：给 key 设的过期时间，管新鲜度而非容量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL (Time To Live) is a per-key expiry that governs freshness, not capacity.

optionExplanations: FIFO 只看谁最早进来，识别不了长期赢家。
只用 TTL 管过期、不管满了删谁。
对：有一批长期持续热门 key 时，LFU 按频次留住赢家。
随机淘汰可能把长期赢家一并删掉。
optionExplanations_en: FIFO only tracks arrival and can't spot long-term winners.
TTL alone handles expiry, not what to drop when full.
Right: with persistently popular keys, LFU keeps winners by frequency.
Random eviction may drop long-term winners too.

q: LRU 和 LFU 的核心区别维度是？
q_en: What is the core dimension that separates LRU from LFU?
scenario: 新闻缓存内存有限：既有突发几小时的爆款，也有连续几周被读的长期热门文章。
scenario_en: A news cache has limited memory and holds both stories that spike for a few hours and evergreen ones read for weeks.
options: LRU 看累计访问频次，LFU 看最近访问时间
LRU 看最近访问时间，LFU 看访问频次
两者都只按插入时间淘汰
两者完全等价、没有区别
why: LRU 按「最近有没有被用」淘汰（recency），LFU 按「被用了多少次」淘汰（frequency）。前者适应近期热点，后者保留长期赢家。
why_en: LRU evicts by recency of access while LFU evicts by frequency of access.
options_en: LRU tracks cumulative frequency; LFU tracks recency of access.
LRU tracks recency of access; LFU tracks frequency of access.
Both only track insertion time.
They are completely equivalent.
tradeoff: 最近使用时间 recency（LRU） vs 访问频次 frequency（LFU）

termDefinitions.meaning: 全称 Least Recently Used：按最近访问时间淘汰（recency）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LRU (Least Recently Used) evicts by recency of access.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全称 Least Frequently Used：按累计访问频次淘汰（frequency）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LFU (Least Frequently Used) evicts by frequency of access.

termDefinitions.meaning: 以‘最近有没有被用过’为淘汰依据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Recency evicts based on how recently a key was used.

termDefinitions.meaning: 以‘一共被用过多少次’为淘汰依据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Frequency evicts based on how many times a key was used.

optionExplanations: 说反了：LRU 看最近时间，LFU 才看累计频次。
对：LRU 看最近是否用过，LFU 看用过多少次。
错：只按插入时间是 FIFO，不是 LRU/LFU。
错：两者优化目标不同，并不等价。
optionExplanations_en: Backwards: LRU tracks recency; LFU tracks cumulative frequency.
Right: LRU by whether it was used recently; LFU by how many times.
Wrong: insertion-time-only is FIFO, not LRU/LFU.
Wrong: they optimize for different things and aren't equivalent.

q: 关于 FIFO 淘汰策略，正确的是？
q_en: Which statement about FIFO eviction is correct?
scenario: 一个嵌入式设备上的小缓存只有 4MB 内存和很紧的 CPU 预算，不想为每个 key 维护访问统计。
scenario_en: An embedded cache has 4MB of memory and a tight CPU budget, so it can't track per-key access statistics.
options: 按访问频次的高低来淘汰 key
只按插入时间淘汰最老的，可能删掉仍很热的数据
和 LRU 完全等价，行为一致
是真实系统里最常用的淘汰策略
why: FIFO 只看谁最早进来，用一个简单队列即可，但它忽略访问模式，可能把还很热的数据淘汰掉，所以真实系统里很少单独用。
why_en: FIFO evicts the oldest by insertion time only, ignoring usage, so it may drop still-hot data and is rarely used in real systems.
options_en: Evicts keys by access frequency.
Evicts the oldest by insertion time only, so it can drop still-hot data.
Equivalent to LRU, with identical behavior.
It is the most common eviction policy in real systems.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全称 First In First Out：按插入顺序淘汰最早进来的 key，不看使用模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FIFO (First In First Out) evicts the earliest-inserted key regardless of usage.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全称 Least Recently Used：按最近访问时间淘汰。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LRU (Least Recently Used) evicts by recency of access.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全称 Least Frequently Used：按访问频次淘汰。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LFU (Least Frequently Used) evicts by frequency of access.

optionExplanations: 错：按访问频次是 LFU 的做法，不是 FIFO。
对：只按进入顺序、不看使用模式，正是 FIFO 的定义。
错：LRU 看访问时间，FIFO 不看，两者不等价。
错：最常用的是 LRU；FIFO 因识别不了热点很少单用。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: evicting by frequency is LFU, not FIFO.
Right: evicting purely by arrival order regardless of usage is exactly FIFO.
Wrong: LRU tracks access time, FIFO doesn't, so they aren't equivalent.
Wrong: LRU is the common default; FIFO is rarely used alone since it can't spot hot keys.

scenario: Cache 里既有 10 分钟后过期的 user profile，也有不过期的热门榜单；现在内存快满了。
scenario_en: The cache has user profiles expiring in ten minutes and a hot leaderboard with no expiry; now memory is almost full.
q: 关于 TTL，下面哪种说法最准确？
q_en: Which statement about TTL is most accurate?
options: TTL 是一种独立的淘汰策略，可直接替代 LRU/LFU
TTL 不是淘汰策略，只给 key 设过期，常配 LRU/LFU
TTL 只能用在 CDN 边缘缓存的场景
设了 TTL 之后就不再需要任何淘汰策略
why: TTL 会删 key，但回答的是「何时过期」，不是内存满时「删谁」。TTL 管新鲜度，LRU/LFU 管容量。
why_en: TTL can delete keys, but it answers when a key expires, not which key to drop when memory is full. Pair it with LRU/LFU for capacity control.
options_en: TTL is a standalone eviction policy that directly replaces LRU/LFU.
TTL is not an eviction policy; it sets a per-key expiry and pairs with LRU/LFU.
TTL only works for CDN edge caching.
With a TTL you no longer need any eviction policy.
tradeoff: 时间过期 vs 容量淘汰
whenOtherWins: 想优先删快过期的 key 时，用 TTL-aware eviction。

termDefinitions.meaning: key 到达设定时间后逻辑失效，不应再被读到；Redis 可在访问时删除，也会后台主动清理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Expiration invalidates a key after its configured time, such as SET key value EX 600.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存空间不够时，系统选择删除哪些 key 来腾内存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eviction chooses which keys to remove when the cache needs memory.

termDefinitions.meaning: 淘汰时参考剩余 TTL，例如优先删快过期的 key；TTL 是信号，不是完整策略。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL-aware eviction uses remaining TTL as a signal, such as dropping soon-to-expire keys first.

diagram:
flowchart LR
    TTL["TTL"] --> Time["Time reached"]
    Time --> Gone["Logically missing"]
    Gone --> Cleanup["Lazy or active delete"]
    LRU["LRU/LFU"] --> Full["Memory full"]
    Full --> Victim["Evict victim key"]
codeSample:
# TTL + LRU: expiration and eviction are two separate triggers
CONFIG SET maxmemory 2gb
CONFIG SET maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru
SET user:123:profile '{...}' EX 600

# Case 1: 600s passes first -> key is logically expired; GET should miss
GET user:123:profile

# Case 2: memory fills before 600s -> LRU may evict it earlier
# TTL controls freshness; LRU controls capacity.

# TTL + LFU: memory pressure evicts least frequently used instead
CONFIG SET maxmemory-policy allkeys-lfu
SET product:999:detail '{...}' EX 300

# allkeys-lru/lfu: any key can be evicted when full
# volatile-lru/lfu: only keys with TTL are eviction candidates
optionExplanations: 错：TTL 管何时过期，替代不了满了删谁。
对：TTL 只设过期管新鲜度，容量靠 LRU/LFU。
错：应用缓存、会话、API 响应都常用 TTL。
错：未过期 key 一多仍会占满内存。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: TTL governs when to expire, not what to drop when full.
Right: TTL only sets expiry for freshness; capacity needs LRU/LFU.
Wrong: app caches, sessions, and API responses use TTL too.
Wrong: many unexpired keys can still fill memory.

scenario: 缓存的是第三方 API 响应和会话令牌，这类数据必须在一段时间后自动刷新/失效。
scenario_en: The cache stores third-party API responses and session tokens, and this data must refresh or expire automatically after some time.
q: 最该配置的是？
q_en: What should you configure first?
options: 给这些 key 设置 TTL 过期时间
把淘汰策略改成 FIFO
关闭所有淘汰策略、永不过期
把写模式改成 Write-Behind
why: 当数据「必须最终刷新」时，TTL 是必备：API 响应、会话令牌到期自动失效，下次读再拉新值，天然限制了陈旧程度。
why_en: When data must eventually refresh, like API responses or session tokens, a TTL is essential so entries expire and get repopulated.
options_en: Set a TTL expiry on these keys.
Switch the eviction policy to FIFO.
Turn off all eviction so nothing expires.
Switch the write mode to write-behind.
whenOtherWins: 写后必须立刻读到新值时，改用写时失效。

termDefinitions.meaning: 全称 Time To Live：给 key 设的过期时间，到点自动失效、下次读回源刷新。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL (Time To Live) is a per-key expiry after which the key lapses and refetches on the next read.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全称 First In First Out：按插入顺序淘汰，管容量而非过期刷新。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FIFO (First In First Out) evicts by insertion order, addressing capacity, not scheduled refresh.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写只落缓存、异步批量刷库，是写侧优化，不解决读侧过期。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write-behind writes to cache and flushes async; it optimizes writes, not read-side expiry.

codeSample:
# 数据必须定期刷新：写入即带过期，到点自动失效
SET session:abc123 '{...}' EX 3600     # 会话令牌 1h 后过期
SET api:weather:94107 '{...}' EX 300   # 第三方响应 5min 后刷新
GET api:weather:94107                   # 过期后 miss -> 回源重新拉取并回填
# EX = 秒级 TTL；到点 key 逻辑失效，下次读自然取到新值
optionExplanations: 对：数据必须定期刷新时，TTL 到点失效、下次读拉新值。
FIFO 管容量淘汰，解决不了到期刷新。
关掉淘汰会让陈旧数据一直留着。
Write-Behind 是写侧模式，管不了读侧过期。
optionExplanations_en: Right: when data must refresh on a schedule, TTL lapses and the next read refetches.
FIFO handles capacity eviction, not scheduled refresh.
Disabling eviction keeps stale data forever.
Write-behind is write-side and can't expire read-side data.
tradeoff: 到期自动刷新 vs 写后立即新鲜

scenario: 首页 feed 缓存 TTL 60 秒，到 12:01:00 同一瞬间过期，成百上千请求同时未命中、一起冲向数据库，可能把库打垮。
scenario_en: The home feed cache has a 60-second TTL; at 12:01:00 it expires, hundreds or thousands of requests miss at once, and they all rush the DB.
q: 这是什么问题，最有效的解法是？
q_en: What problem is this, and what is the best fix?
options: 热 key 问题；把 key 复制分摊
缓存穿透；加布隆过滤器拦截
缓存击穿/惊群；请求合并单飞
双写不一致；上分布式事务
why: 这是缓存击穿/惊群：同一 key 过期瞬间大量并发 miss 重建。single flight 按 key 合并成一次重建，其余等结果。
why_en: This is a cache stampede. Single flight coalesces by cache key: concurrent misses for feed:home share one rebuild, while different keys do not merge.
options_en: Hot-key problem; replicate the key.
Cache penetration; add a Bloom filter.
Cache stampede / thundering herd; request coalescing (single flight).
Dual-write problem; use a distributed transaction.
tradeoff: 按 key 单飞挡住重建洪峰 vs 等待者仍要等那次慢重建
whenOtherWins: 是持续热 key 而非过期瞬间时，用复制/本地缓存。
diagram:
flowchart LR
    A["GET feed:home miss"] --> K["inflight[feed:home]"]
    B["GET feed:home miss"] --> K
    C["GET user:42 miss"] --> U["inflight[user:42]"]
    K --> One["one rebuild"]
    One --> W["all feed waiters receive result"]
codeSample:
inflight = Map()

get(key):
  v = cache.get(key)
  if v != nil:
    return v

  if inflight.has(key):
    return await inflight[key]

  promise = rebuild_and_fill_cache(key)
  inflight[key] = promise
  try:
    return await promise
  finally:
    inflight.delete(key)

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一个 key 的并发 miss 只让一个请求真正回源或重建，其余请求等待同一个结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Single flight lets only one concurrent miss for the same key rebuild or fetch from the backend; the rest wait for the same result.

termDefinitions.meaning: 判断能不能合并的键，通常就是 cache key 或规范化后的 request fingerprint；不同用户、参数、权限导致结果不同就不能合并。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The coalescing key decides what can merge, usually a cache key or normalized request fingerprint; different users, parameters, or permissions should not merge if the result differs.

optionExplanations: 热 key 是持续超高流量；这里是过期瞬间的重建洪峰。
布隆过滤器挡不存在的 key，但这 key 存在。
对：过期瞬间的并发重建，单飞按 key 合并成一次。
题里没有写冲突，分布式事务无谓增复杂度。
optionExplanations_en: Hot-key is sustained traffic; here it's a rebuild burst at expiry.
A Bloom filter blocks nonexistent keys, but this one exists.
Right: a rebuild burst at expiry; single-flight coalesces per key into one.
There's no write conflict; a distributed transaction only adds complexity.

scenario: 首页 feed 是热点 key。方案 A 用 TTL=60s；方案 B 是用户一发新帖就立刻删除 feed cache。
scenario_en: The home feed is a hot key. Plan A uses TTL=60s; Plan B deletes the feed cache immediately whenever a user posts.
q: 关于「缓存预热」（cache warming）防击穿，正确的是？
q_en: Which statement about cache warming to prevent stampedes is correct?
options: 对所有失效方式都同样有效、都能挡住
只对 TTL 过期有效；写时失效时预热挡不住
预热本身会导致缓存数据不一致
预热本质上就等于请求合并这一手段
why: 预热只挡可预测的 TTL 过期；写时失效是写完立刻 delete、不等 TTL，挡不住第一波 miss。
why_en: Warming refreshes before a known expiry. Write-time invalidation deletes cache right after a write, not when TTL expires; periodic warming only narrows the cold window.
options_en: It works equally for every kind of invalidation.
Only for TTL expiry; if you invalidate on writes, warming can't stop it.
Warming itself causes cache data inconsistency.
Warming is essentially the same as request coalescing.
tradeoff: 可预测过期 vs 突发删除
whenOtherWins: 写时失效要靠请求合并、锁、SWR、限流或写后异步回填来挡第一波。

termDefinitions.meaning: 在用户请求到来前，主动把热点数据加载或刷新进缓存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cache warming proactively loads or refreshes hot data before user requests need it.

termDefinitions.meaning: key 到达预设时间后自动失效；时间点可预测。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL expiry invalidates a key at a configured time, so the expiry point is predictable.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据被写入或修改时立刻删除相关缓存；发生时间取决于用户写入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write-time invalidation deletes related cache entries when data changes, so timing depends on writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按固定间隔刷新热点 key；能缩短写删后的空窗，但不能保证刚删完那一刻有缓存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Periodic warming refreshes hot keys on a fixed interval; it can shorten the cold window but cannot guarantee coverage right after deletion.

diagram:
flowchart TD
    A["TTL=60s"] --> B["55s: warm first"]
    B --> C["60s: users still hit"]
    X["User writes now"] --> Y["delete cache now"]
    Y --> Z["next reads miss together"]
codeSample:
# TTL expiry: predictable, so warming can run before expiry
schedule.every(55).seconds.do(lambda: cache.set("feed:home", db.build_feed(), ttl=60))

# Write-time invalidation: user writes can delete any time; TTL is not checked
def create_post(user_id, post):
    db.insert_post(user_id, post)
    cache.delete("feed:home")      # immediate cold window starts now

# Periodic warming later may refill, but first readers still need protection
schedule.every(60).seconds.do(lambda: cache.set("feed:home", db.build_feed(), ttl=60))
# Use single-flight/lock/stale-while-revalidate for the first miss wave.
optionExplanations: 错：写时删除时机不可预测，预热挡不住那波 miss。
对：预热只能提前覆盖已知的过期时间；写时删除挡不住。
错：不一致来自陈旧/双写，预热做对反而更新鲜。
错：预热是事前刷新，请求合并是并发时挡，不是一回事。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: write-time deletion is unpredictable, so warming can't stop that miss wave.
Right: warming only covers a known expiry time ahead; write-time deletion escapes it.
Wrong: inconsistency comes from staleness/dual writes; done right, warming keeps data fresher.
Wrong: warming refreshes before; coalescing blocks during concurrency — not the same.

q: 「大多数系统读缓存、但写时先写数据库」会直接导致什么问题？
q_en: What problem follows directly when most systems read from cache but write to the database first?
scenario: 用户改完头像先写 MySQL，头像读路径走 Redis，TTL 10 分钟，产品要求改完立刻可见。
scenario_en: Avatar updates are written to MySQL while reads come from Redis with a ten-minute TTL, and the product wants the change visible right away.
options: 有一段窗口缓存仍是旧值，与数据库不一致
每次写入都会当场直接失败、根本无法完成落库
缓存会永远保持为空、从不回填
数据库的读写会被完全绕过
why: 写先落库、缓存还没更新，就有一段窗口缓存是旧值——比如用户换了头像，别人还看到旧头像。这就是缓存一致性问题，只能按新鲜度要求选策略。
why_en: Because systems read from cache but write to the database first, there is a window where the cache holds stale data.
options_en: There is a window where the cache holds the old value, so cache and DB disagree.
Every write fails outright on the spot and can never reach the DB.
The cache stays empty forever and never backfills.
The database reads and writes are completely bypassed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存里的旧值和数据库里的新值暂时不一致。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Stale data is a cached value that temporarily disagrees with the newer value in the database.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写数据后主动删除或更新对应缓存，让下次读拿到新值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cache invalidation deletes or updates the cached entry after a write so the next read is fresh.

optionExplanations: 对：写先落库、缓存没更新，就有一段窗口读到旧值（如旧头像）。
错：写正常成功，问题是缓存还没跟上，不是写失败。
错：下次读 miss 就回填，不会永远为空。
错：读仍走缓存、写仍落库，只是暂时不一致，不是绕过。
optionExplanations_en: Right: DB write first with cache not updated leaves a window of stale reads (like an old avatar).
Wrong: the write succeeds; the issue is the cache lags, not a failed write.
Wrong: the next read miss backfills, so it isn't empty forever.
Wrong: reads still use cache and writes still hit the DB — briefly inconsistent, not bypassed.

q: 处理缓存一致性（stale）问题的常见手段有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which common techniques handle stale-cache consistency problems? (Select all)
scenario: 商品库存页读走缓存、写只更新数据库，要求秒级看到新值，同时不能牺牲读吞吐。
scenario_en: An inventory page reads from cache while writes only touch the DB; new values must show up within seconds without hurting read throughput.
options: 写数据库后删除对应缓存条目（写时失效），下次读回填新值
设置较短的 TTL，容忍短暂陈旧
对 feed/指标/分析类数据直接接受最终一致
给每次读加分布式锁串行化
why: 没有完美方案，按新鲜度要求选：写时失效（最常用）、短 TTL、或对 feed/指标直接接受最终一致。给每次读加分布式锁会毁掉缓存的性能，不是常规解。
why_en: Common fixes are invalidating the cache on writes, using short TTLs, or accepting eventual consistency for feeds and metrics.
options_en: Delete the cache entry after writing the DB (write-time invalidation); refill on next read.
Use a short TTL and tolerate brief staleness.
Accept eventual consistency for feed/metrics/analytics data.
Put a distributed lock on every read to serialize it.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Write["Write DB"] --> Invalidate["Delete cache"]
    Invalidate --> Next["Next read"]
    Next --> Fill["Refill fresh value"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 写数据后立刻删除对应缓存条目，下次读回填新值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write-time invalidation deletes the matching cache entry right after a write so the next read backfills.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全称 Time To Live：给 key 设的过期时间；短 TTL 把陈旧上限压到过期时长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL (Time To Live) caps staleness at the expiry length when kept short.

termDefinitions.meaning: 允许缓存短暂落后，最终会收敛到数据库的最新值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventual consistency allows the cache to lag briefly and converge to the latest DB value.

termDefinitions.meaning: 跨进程串行化访问的锁；给每次读都加会拖垮吞吐。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A distributed lock serializes access across processes; using it on every read wrecks throughput.

optionExplanations: 对：写后删缓存、下次读回填新值，是最常用的失效手段。
对：短 TTL 把陈旧上限压到过期时长，简单可控。
对：feed/指标/分析不需强一致，接受最终一致能简化架构。
错：每次读都加分布式锁会摧毁缓存吞吐，不是常规解。
optionExplanations_en: True: delete cache after a write and backfill on next read — the most common invalidation.
True: a short TTL caps staleness at the expiry length, simple and controllable.
True: feeds/metrics/analytics don't need strong consistency, so eventual consistency simplifies things.
False: a distributed lock per read destroys cache throughput and isn't a standard fix.

scenario: 做 Twitter，所有人都在看 Taylor Swift 的资料，key `user:taylorswift` 每秒数百万请求，即使命中率很高，单个 Redis 节点/分片也被这一个 key 压垮。
scenario_en: In a Twitter-like system, everyone is viewing Taylor Swift's profile, and key `user:taylorswift` gets millions of requests per second, overloading one Redis node or shard despite a high hit rate.
q: 这是什么问题？
q_en: What problem is this?
options: 缓存击穿（过期瞬间）
热 key（hot key）问题
双写不一致
内存碎片
why: 这是热 key：单个 key 的流量远超其他，即便命中率高，也会把承载它的那一个节点/分片打满，成为瓶颈。
why_en: This is a hot-key problem: one key gets vastly more traffic than others and overloads the single node or shard holding it.
options_en: Cache stampede (at the expiry instant).
Hot-key problem.
Dual-write inconsistency.
Memory fragmentation.
tradeoff: 复制/分摊持续高流量 vs 单点承载
whenOtherWins: 若是过期瞬间同时重建同一 key，那是击穿，用请求合并。

termDefinitions.meaning: 被访问频率远超其他 key 的缓存键，会压垮承载它的单个节点或分片。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hot key gets far more traffic than others and can overload the single node or shard holding it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一 key 过期瞬间大量并发 miss 一起重建、冲击后端。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cache stampede is many concurrent misses rebuilding the same key right after it expires.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存数据按 key 分布到的一个节点/分区；一个 key 只落在一个分片上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A shard is one node/partition that holds a subset of keys; a given key lives on exactly one shard.

optionExplanations: 击穿是过期瞬间并发重建；这里 key 一直命中。
对：单个 key 流量碾压其他，把它所在节点/分片打满。
双写讲缓存与库不一致，与单点压垮无关。
内存碎片是内存管理问题，不是这里症状。
optionExplanations_en: Stampede is concurrent rebuild at expiry; here the key keeps hitting.
Right: one key's traffic dwarfs others and saturates its node/shard.
Dual-write is about inconsistency, not one key overloading a node.
Memory fragmentation is a memory-management issue, not this.

q: 缓解热 key 的常见手段有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which techniques commonly mitigate hot keys? (Select all)
scenario: 明星发文让单个 key 每秒被读 50 万次，全部哈希到同一个 Redis 分片，该分片 CPU 打满。
scenario_en: A celebrity post drives 500k reads a second at one key, all hashing to a single Redis shard whose CPU is pinned.
options: 把热 key 复制到多个缓存节点，读请求负载均衡分摊
把极热的值放进程内缓存做本地兜底，减少打 Redis
对特定 key 的滥用流量做限流
给这个 key 设更长的 TTL
why: 热 key 靠「分摊流量」：多节点复制 + 负载均衡、进程内本地兜底、对滥用限流。加长 TTL 只影响新鲜度，不能分摊单节点的流量压力。
why_en: Hot keys are mitigated by replicating the key across nodes, adding a local in-process fallback, and rate-limiting abusive traffic.
options_en: Replicate the hot key across nodes and load-balance the reads.
Put the very hot value in an in-process cache as a local fallback to spare Redis.
Rate-limit abusive traffic to that key.
Give the key a longer TTL.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Hot["Hot key"] --> Rep["Replicate key"]
    Hot --> Local["Local cache"]
    Hot --> Limit["Rate limit abuse"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 被访问频率远超其他 key 的缓存键，需要把流量分摊开。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hot key receives far more traffic than others and must have its load spread out.

termDefinitions.meaning: 存在应用进程内存里的本地缓存，读最快、可做热点兜底。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An in-process cache lives in the app's memory, giving the fastest reads and a local fallback.

termDefinitions.meaning: 限制某来源或某 key 的请求速率，挡住滥用流量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A rate limit caps the request rate from a source or to a key, blocking abusive traffic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全称 Time To Live：key 的过期时间，管新鲜度而非分摊流量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL (Time To Live) is a key's expiry; it governs freshness, not load spreading.

optionExplanations: 对：把热 key 复制到多节点+负载均衡，摊开单节点流量。
对：把极热值放进程内本地兜底，减少打 Redis。
对：对某 key 的滥用流量限流，保护热点节点。
错：加长 TTL 只改新鲜度，分摊不了当前的流量压力。
optionExplanations_en: True: replicate the hot key across nodes with load balancing to spread single-node traffic.
True: put the very hot value in-process as a local fallback to spare Redis.
True: rate-limit abusive traffic to that key to protect the hot node.
False: a longer TTL only changes freshness and can't spread the current load.

q: 如果 Redis 突然宕机，最需要预先设计的是什么，以免数据库被瞬间流量压垮？
q_en: If Redis suddenly goes down, what should be designed ahead of time so the database is not crushed by instant traffic?
scenario: 读 QPS 30 万，98% 命中 Redis；数据库只扛得住 2 万 QPS，Redis 集群整体不可用。
scenario_en: You take 300k reads a second with a 98% Redis hit rate, but the database only survives 20k QPS, and the Redis cluster goes down.
options: 回退到数据库，并加熔断/限流防止把库打垮
直接给所有用户返回错误、不做降级
无脑重试 Redis 直到它自己彻底恢复为止
直接把整个线上服务关闭掉
why: Redis 挂掉后所有读都回退到数据库，可能形成突发洪峰。要提前加熔断器/限流避免打垮库，必要时留一层进程内缓存做最后兜底。
why_en: If Redis goes down, requests fall back to the database, so add circuit breakers or rate limits to avoid crushing it.
options_en: Fall back to the DB with a circuit breaker / rate limit so it isn't crushed.
Just return an error to every user with no fallback.
Blindly retry Redis until it fully recovers on its own.
Shut the whole live service down.

termDefinitions.meaning: 下游过载或失败率过高时快速失败/降级，避免把它压垮。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A circuit breaker fails fast or degrades when a dependency is overloaded, preventing it from being crushed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 限制打向数据库的请求速率，削平缓存宕机后的突发洪峰。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A rate limit caps requests to the database, flattening the surge after a cache outage.

termDefinitions.meaning: 主路径失效时退到备用路径（如查库、本地兜底）以保持部分可用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A fallback drops to a backup path (such as the DB or a local cache) to keep partial availability.

optionExplanations: 对：Redis 挂后读回退查库，靠熔断/限流削平洪峰、保住库。
对所有用户返回错误等于放弃可用性，应有降级。
无脑重试会把库和 Redis 一起拖垮，形成雪崩。
关停整个服务是过度反应，比降级严重得多。
optionExplanations_en: Right: after Redis dies, reads fall back to the DB; a breaker/rate limit flattens the surge and saves it.
Erroring to all users abandons availability; there should be graceful degradation.
Blind retries drag the DB and Redis down together into a cascade.
Shutting the whole service down is an overreaction, far worse than degrading.

q: 在「未命中时由谁去查数据库」上，Cache-Aside 和 Read-Through 的区别是？
q_en: For cache misses, how do cache-aside and read-through differ on who queries the database?
scenario: 同一份缓存被 Java 和 Go 两种服务读取，团队在争论 miss 时该由谁去查数据库、谁回填。
scenario_en: Java and Go services share one cache, and the team is arguing over who queries the DB and repopulates on a miss.
options: 两者在未命中时都由缓存层自己去查库并回填
前者由应用查库回填，后者由缓存自己查库
两者未命中时都由应用去查库回填
两者其实都不需要去查数据库
why: Cache-Aside 的 miss 逻辑在应用（应用查库回填）；Read-Through 把它下沉到缓存，应用只跟缓存交互。
why_en: In cache-aside the application fetches from the database and populates the cache, while in read-through the cache itself does the fetch and fill.
options_en: Both let the cache layer itself query the DB and backfill on a miss.
Cache-aside: the app queries the DB and backfills; read-through: the cache does it.
Both let the app query the DB and backfill on a miss.
Neither actually needs to query the database.
tradeoff: 应用代码管未命中（Cache-Aside） vs 缓存层管未命中（Read-Through）

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用先查缓存，未命中时由应用查库并回填缓存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: In cache-aside the app checks cache and, on a miss, queries the DB and backfills.

termDefinitions.meaning: 未命中时由缓存层自己查库并回填，应用只跟缓存交互。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: In read-through the cache queries the DB and fills itself on a miss; the app only talks to the cache.

optionExplanations: 错：Cache-Aside 的查库在应用里，不是缓存查。
对：Cache-Aside 由应用查库回填；读穿透把这步下沉缓存。
错：Read-Through 由缓存层查库，不是应用查。
错：miss 时总得有人查库，只是位置不同。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: cache-aside's DB query lives in the app, not the cache.
Right: cache-aside has the app query and backfill; read-through pushes it into the cache.
Wrong: read-through has the cache query the DB, not the app.
Wrong: on a miss someone must query the DB; they differ only in where.

q: 把「给数据库前面加缓存」的决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the decision chain for adding a cache in front of a database in the right order:
steps: 需求：读多写少、热点数据被反复读、数据库成为瓶颈
代价：缓存可能返回旧数据（与库不一致）
缓解：TTL + 写时失效，把陈旧程度控制住
why: 一条合格的决策 = 需求（读多、热点重复读）→ 选型（Redis + Cache-Aside）→ 代价（陈旧/不一致）→ 缓解（TTL + 写时失效）。面试考的就是你能把这条链讲清楚。
why_en: A solid decision runs requirement, choice, cost, then mitigation: read-heavy hot reads lead to a Redis cache, which risks staleness, bounded by TTL and write-time invalidation.
diagram:
flowchart LR R["需求：读多写少
热点反复读、DB 瓶颈"] --> C["选型：Redis + Cache-Aside"] C --> K["代价：可能读到旧数据"] K --> M["缓解：TTL + 写时失效"]

q: 把面试里系统性引入缓存的步骤排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the steps for introducing caching systematically in an interview in the right order:
steps: 先定位瓶颈：具体哪个查询慢、DB 负载高在哪
决定缓存什么（读频繁、少变、贵的数据）
正视缺点（失效、缓存宕机、击穿）
why: 面试引入缓存的顺序：定位瓶颈 → 决定缓存什么 → 选架构 → 设淘汰 → 谈缺点。先证明「为什么需要」，再谈「怎么做」和「哪里会出问题」。
why_en: Introduce caching by first identifying the bottleneck, then deciding what to cache, choosing the architecture, setting eviction, and finally addressing the downsides.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Bottleneck["Find bottleneck"] --> What["Choose hot data"]
    What --> Mode["Cache-Aside"]
    Mode --> Policy["LRU + TTL"]
    Policy --> Risks["Invalidation + outage"]

scenario: 面试刚开始画完高层架构，还没分析读写负载和延迟。
scenario_en: At the start of an interview, you have just drawn the high-level architecture and have not analyzed read/write load or latency yet.
q: 关于什么时候提缓存，正确的做法是？
q_en: When should you bring up caching in an interview?
options: 一上来就加缓存，越早加进架构越好
先定位数据库瓶颈、用粗略数字量化，再加缓存
永远不要主动提起缓存，等别人说
只有等面试官明确问到了才提缓存
why: 别一上来就加缓存。先指出具体瓶颈——读多、查询贵、DB CPU 高、或有低延迟要求——用粗略数字量化，再说明缓存怎么解决。先「为什么」后「怎么做」。
why_en: Do not jump to caching; first identify a database bottleneck, quantify it with rough numbers, and then explain how a cache solves it.
options_en: Add a cache right away — the earlier it goes into the design, the better.
First pinpoint the DB bottleneck, quantify it roughly, then add caching.
Never bring up caching yourself; wait for someone else.
Only mention caching if the interviewer explicitly asks.
tradeoff: 先证明瓶颈再加缓存 vs 过早优化
whenOtherWins: 良好索引的 DB 就能满足负载时，别为加而加。

termDefinitions.meaning: 限制系统整体吞吐或延迟的那个最紧的环节（如 DB CPU 高、慢查询）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A bottleneck is the tightest constraint limiting overall throughput or latency, such as high DB CPU or slow queries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 还没证明瓶颈就先加复杂度（如缓存），常带来不必要的成本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Premature optimization adds complexity like caching before proving a bottleneck, often at needless cost.

optionExplanations: 一上来就加缓存是过早优化，还没证明瓶颈。
对：先用粗略数字点名 DB 瓶颈，再讲缓存怎么解。
缓存值得在有瓶颈时主动提，不该回避。
等面试官问显得被动，应主动识别问题。
optionExplanations_en: Adding a cache upfront is premature optimization before proving a bottleneck.
Right: name the DB bottleneck with rough numbers, then show how caching solves it.
Caching is worth raising when there's a bottleneck, not avoiding.
Waiting to be asked looks passive; spot problems yourself.

scenario: 用 Redis 缓存用户资料，key 为 user:123:profile，希望 10 分钟后自动过期以限制陈旧。
scenario_en: You use Redis to cache user profile key `user:123:profile` and want it to expire automatically after 10 minutes to bound staleness.
q: 哪条命令能「写入值并设置 10 分钟过期」？
q_en: Which command writes the value and sets a 10-minute expiry?
options: SET user:123:profile <json>
SET user:123:profile <json> EX 600
GET user:123:profile
SET user:123:profile <json> EX 10
why: EX 600 = 600 秒 = 10 分钟过期。只 SET 不带 EX 不会过期（易陈旧无上限）；EX 10 只有 10 秒；GET 是读不是写。
why_en: Use SET with EX 600 to store the value and expire it after ten minutes, bounding staleness.
options_en: SET user:123:profile <json>
SET user:123:profile <json> EX 600
GET user:123:profile
SET user:123:profile <json> EX 10
tradeoff: 设 TTL 有界陈旧 vs 不设 TTL 无限期缓存
codeSample:
# 写入用户资料并设 10 分钟 TTL
SET user:123:profile '{"name":"..."}' EX 600
# 读取（Cache-Aside：未命中再查库回填）
GET user:123:profile

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 写命令，把值写入指定 key，可附带过期参数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SET is the Redis write command that stores a value at a key, optionally with an expiry.

termDefinitions.meaning: SET 的过期参数，单位秒；EX 600 表示 600 秒后过期。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: EX is SET's expiry argument in seconds; EX 600 means the key expires after 600 seconds.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 读命令，返回 key 的当前值，不写入也不设过期。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GET is the Redis read command returning a key's current value; it neither writes nor sets expiry.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全称 Time To Live：key 的过期时间，到点自动失效以限制陈旧。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL (Time To Live) is a key's expiry that lapses automatically to bound staleness.

optionExplanations: 不带 EX 的 SET 永不过期，资料会无限期陈旧。
对：SET … EX 600 写入值并设 600 秒=10 分钟过期。
GET 是读命令，既不写入也设不了过期。
EX 10 只有 10 秒，太短，会频繁 miss 回源。
optionExplanations_en: SET without EX never expires, so the profile stays stale indefinitely.
Right: SET … EX 600 writes the value and expires it after 600s = 10 minutes.
GET is a read command; it neither writes nor sets expiry.
EX 10 is only 10 seconds — too short, causing frequent miss-and-refetch.

q: 补全「为什么缓存计算好的个性化 feed」这条推理：
q_en: Fill in the reasoning for caching a computed personalized feed:
text: 我们缓存计算好的 feed，因为它计算{{昂贵}}（要跨多表 join）、被{{反复}}读取、且能容忍{{短暂陈旧}}（最终一致），所以缓存 60 秒、用 Redis 1ms 返回。
why: 这是一条 reasoning-cloze：贵 + 读多 + 容忍陈旧 = 缓存的黄金三条件。个性化 feed 正好三者都满足，所以值得缓存并设短 TTL。
why_en: We cache the computed feed because it is expensive to build, read repeatedly, and tolerant of brief staleness, so a short-TTL cache serves it in about a millisecond.

scenario: 要决定「缓存什么」。有四类数据：用户资料（每次页面加载都读、很少改）、一次性支付回执、实时精确库存数、随机生成的验证码。
scenario_en: You are deciding what to cache among user profiles, one-time payment receipts, exact real-time inventory counts, and random verification codes.
q: 最该优先缓存的是？
q_en: What should be cached first?
options: 随机生成、只用一次的短信验证码
用户资料：读频繁、少变、每次加载都要
必须实时精确的库存计数
只读一次的支付回执凭证
why: 缓存的黄金标准：读频繁、少变、获取/计算贵。用户资料完全符合；验证码一次性、库存要精确强一致、支付回执一次性，都不该缓存。
why_en: Cache data that is read frequently, changes rarely, and is expensive to fetch, like user profiles, and avoid one-off or strongly-consistent data.
options_en: A randomly generated, single-use SMS verification code.
User profiles: read often, rarely change, needed on every load.
Real-time exact inventory counts that must be precise.
A one-time payment receipt read only once.
tradeoff: 读多/少变/取贵（该缓存） vs 一次性或强一致（不缓存）
whenOtherWins: 库存可容忍近似展示时也能缓存，但下单扣减必须走强一致 DB。

termDefinitions.meaning: 读到的永远是最新写入值；库存扣减这类路径需要它，不能靠缓存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Strong consistency means reads always see the latest write; inventory decrement needs it and cannot rely on cache.

termDefinitions.meaning: 适合缓存的数据同时满足：读频繁、变化少、获取/计算贵。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The golden criteria for caching: data that is read often, changes rarely, and is expensive to fetch.

optionExplanations: 验证码一次性，缓存无命中收益还有安全风险。
对：用户资料读频繁、少变、取贵，正中缓存黄金三条件。
库存要强一致，缓存会给旧值导致超卖。
支付回执只读一次，缓存留着没人再读。
optionExplanations_en: A one-time code has no hit benefit and adds security risk.
Right: user profiles are read often, rarely change, and are expensive — the golden criteria.
Inventory needs strong consistency; a stale count risks overselling.
A payment receipt is read once, so a cached copy is never reused.

scenario: Strava 这类运动 App，用户在没有网络的偏远地区跑步时仍要记录数据，联网后再同步。
scenario_en: In a Strava-like app, users still need to record run data in remote areas without network and sync later when online.
q: 这体现了哪一层缓存？
q_en: Which cache layer does this represent?
options: CDN 边缘缓存
客户端 / 设备端缓存
外部 Redis 共享缓存
数据库查询结果缓存
why: 把数据存在用户设备上、离线可用、联网再同步，是典型的客户端/设备端缓存。它离请求方最近、省网络调用，但后端对其控制弱、失效更难。
why_en: Keeping run data on the device while offline and syncing later is client-side caching, which is closest to the user but hardest to invalidate.
options_en: CDN cache.
Client-side / on-device cache.
External Redis cache.
Database query cache.
whenOtherWins: 要跨用户共享、后端可控失效的数据，应放服务端 Redis。

termDefinitions.meaning: 把数据存在用户设备本地，离线可读、联网后再同步；离用户最近但后端难以失效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A client-side cache stores data on the user's device for offline reads and later sync; closest to the user but hard for the backend to invalidate.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全称 Content Delivery Network：把公开内容缓存在边缘节点，面向地理分布，不是离线存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN (Content Delivery Network) caches public content on edge nodes for geo distribution, not offline storage.

termDefinitions.meaning: 后端集中式内存缓存，多实例共享；设备离线时连不上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is a backend in-memory cache shared across instances and unreachable while a device is offline.

optionExplanations: CDN 缓存公开静态媒体，解决不了完全离线记录。
对：数据存设备本地、离线可读、联网再同步，正是客户端缓存。
Redis 在后端，设备离线时连不上。
查询结果缓存是服务端概念，与离线无关。
optionExplanations_en: A CDN caches public static media and can't handle fully offline recording.
Right: storing data on-device, readable offline and synced later, is client-side caching.
Redis is backend and unreachable while the device is offline.
Query-result caching is server-side, unrelated to offline.
tradeoff: 离设备最近可离线 vs 跨用户共享可控失效

q: 面试里关于缓存，最该守住的一条整体原则是？
q_en: What overall caching principle should you defend in an interview?
scenario: 面试官指着一个 200 QPS、索引良好、P99 8ms 的查询问：这里要不要加一层缓存？
scenario_en: The interviewer points at a well-indexed query doing 200 QPS at 8ms p99 and asks whether it needs a cache at all.
options: 把所有数据都缓存起来，一律求最快
别什么都缓存，先证明瓶颈值得这份复杂度
缓存越多命中率越高，总是划算的
只要上了 Redis 就不用管数据库索引
why: 缓存的代价是复杂度：陈旧、失效、缓存宕机拖垮库、热 key 瓶颈。要展示你知道「何时值得、何时一个良好索引的数据库就够了」，而不是无脑全缓存。
why_en: Do not cache everything; show you know when caching is worth its complexity and when a well-indexed database is enough.
options_en: Cache all data indiscriminately for maximum speed.
Don't cache everything — first prove a bottleneck worth the complexity.
More caching always means a higher hit rate and is always worth it.
Once Redis is in place you can ignore database indexes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 请求在缓存中直接命中的比例；高不代表一定划算，还要算复杂度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hit rate is the fraction of requests served from cache; high is not automatically worth it once complexity is counted.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按列建立的查找结构，加速查询；与缓存互补，缓存 miss 时仍靠它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A database index is a lookup structure that speeds queries; complementary to cache and still relied on when the cache misses.

optionExplanations: 无脑全缓存会背上陈旧、失效、宕机、热 key 一堆风险。
对：先证明瓶颈值得这份复杂度再加缓存，好索引够用就别加。
命中率高不等于划算，还要算复杂度和失效成本。
缓存与索引互补，缓存 miss 时没索引的库照样慢。
optionExplanations_en: Caching everything takes on staleness, invalidation, outage, and hot-key risks.
Right: prove a bottleneck worth the complexity before caching; skip it when a good index suffices.
A high hit rate isn't automatically worth it; weigh complexity and invalidation cost.
Cache and index are complementary; on a miss, a DB without an index is still slow.

scenario: 峰值时段数据库 CPU 顶到 80%,采样显示几乎全花在一批反复执行的相同读查询上。
scenario_en: At peak the database CPU hits 80%, and profiling shows almost all of it goes to a batch of the same read queries running over and over.
q: 这个信号最支持哪条设计判断?
q_en: Which design judgment does this signal most support?
options: 缓存这批热查询,把数据库负载砍掉七八成
给数据库纵向升配更多 CPU 核心来硬扛峰值负载
再给这些读查询加索引,进一步压低 CPU
把这批读分摊到只读副本上做负载均衡
options_en: Cache these hot queries to cut database load by roughly 70-80%.
Vertically scale the database with more CPU cores to brute-force the peak.
Add more indexes to these read queries to push CPU down further.
Spread these reads across read replicas to balance the load.
why: CPU 全耗在反复执行的相同读上,结果高度可复用;缓存这批热查询直接免掉重复计算,文章估算约砍掉 70-80% 的 DB 负载。升配或加副本仍在让库一遍遍重算同一批结果。
why_en: The CPU is spent re-running identical reads, so the results are highly reusable — caching these hot queries removes that repeated work and cuts DB load by about 70-80%.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库的只读副本,用来分摊读流量;分摊的是不同的读,免不掉重复计算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A read replica is a read-only copy of the database used to spread read traffic, but it still recomputes each query.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给单台机器加更多 CPU/内存来提升容量;治标不治本地缓解重复计算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Vertical scaling adds more CPU or memory to a single machine, which relieves but does not remove repeated work.

optionExplanations: 对:相同读反复跑、结果可复用,缓存热查询免掉重复计算,DB 负载降约七八成。
升配 CPU 只是买时间,库还在一遍遍重算同一批查询,不治本。
这些查询多半已走索引;加索引降不了「重复执行」本身的开销。
只读副本能分摊不同的读;这里是同一批查询反复跑,缓存更对症。
optionExplanations_en: Right: identical reads with reusable results — caching them removes the repeated compute and cuts DB load ~70-80%.
Scaling CPU only buys time; the DB still recomputes the same queries over and over.
These queries are likely already indexed; more indexes don't remove the cost of repeated execution.
Replicas spread different reads; with one repeated batch, caching fits better.

scenario: 产品定了硬性 SLA:API 的 P99 要 <10ms;但底层数据库查询本身就要 30-50ms。
scenario_en: The product sets a hard SLA: API p99 must be under 10ms, but the underlying database query alone takes 30-50ms.
q: 面对这条延迟目标,现实的设计路径是?
q_en: Given this latency target, what is the realistic design path?
options: 把热读放进内存缓存,命中约 1-2ms,压进预算
优化 SQL 与索引,把 30-50ms 的磁盘查询压到 10ms 以下
调大数据库连接池并发,让更多查询同时跑
直接放宽 SLA 到 50ms,反正用户感知不到
options_en: Put hot reads in an in-memory cache at ~1-2ms to fit the budget.
Optimize SQL and indexes to push the 30-50ms disk query under 10ms.
Increase database connection-pool concurrency so more queries run at once.
Just relax the SLA to 50ms since users won't notice.
why: <10ms 是给定的产品 SLA、不是推导结果,而磁盘查询 30-50ms 的地板已经超标;只有内存缓存(约 1-2ms)能把热读压进这个预算。这条 SLA 直接逼出「必须缓存」的路径,代价是陈旧与失效。
why_en: The sub-10ms target is a given SLA, not a derived number, and a 30-50ms disk query already blows it — only an in-memory cache at 1-2ms fits the budget, which is why this SLA forces caching.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全称 Service Level Agreement,服务等级协议:对外承诺的性能/可用性目标,如 P99<10ms。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SLA (Service Level Agreement) is a committed performance or availability target, such as p99 under 10ms.

termDefinitions.meaning: 第 99 百分位延迟:99% 的请求快于这个值,用来衡量尾部延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: P99 is the 99th-percentile latency: 99% of requests are faster than this value, capturing tail latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全称 Structured Query Language,查询关系型数据库的语言。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SQL (Structured Query Language) is the language used to query relational databases.

optionExplanations: 对:只有内存命中 1-2ms 装得进 <10ms;SLA 是给定目标,逼出必须缓存。
索引也逃不掉磁盘访问地板,30-50ms 很难压到个位数毫秒。
加并发提高吞吐,但单条查询延迟不变,P99 还是 30-50ms。
SLA 是产品给定的硬约束,不能为了迁就实现随手放宽。
optionExplanations_en: Right: only an in-memory hit at 1-2ms fits under 10ms; the SLA is given and forces caching.
Indexes can't escape the disk-access floor, so 30-50ms rarely drops to single-digit ms.
More concurrency raises throughput but not per-query latency; p99 stays 30-50ms.
The SLA is a hard product constraint, not something to relax to suit the implementation.

scenario: 首页 feed 是热点 key,TTL 到点瞬间上千请求同时 miss 打到数据库;除了请求合并和预热,还有第三种防击穿手段。
scenario_en: The homepage feed is a hot key; at the TTL expiry thousands of requests miss at once and hit the DB. Besides request coalescing and warming, there is a third stampede defense.
q: 这第三种手段是什么,怎么起作用?
q_en: What is this third technique and how does it work?
options: 概率式提前过期:临近 TTL 时提前异步重建缓存
把 TTL 设为无限大,让这个热点 key 永不过期失效
让所有 key 共用同一到期时刻,到点统一刷新
缓存 miss 时直接返回错误,把重试压力甩给客户端
options_en: Probabilistic early expiration: rebuild the cache asynchronously as the TTL nears.
Set the TTL to infinite so this hot key never expires at all.
Give every key the same expiry instant and refresh them together.
On a miss, return an error and push the retry pressure to the client.
why: 概率式提前过期让 key 越接近 TTL、单个请求越可能被随机选中,提前在后台异步重建缓存;于是真正过期前就有人悄悄刷新,避免所有人卡在同一刻一起 miss。代价:极少数请求要提前重算。
why_en: As a key nears its TTL, probabilistic early expiration lets a request rebuild it in the background before the hard expiry, so no single moment forces everyone to miss.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全称 Time To Live,存活时间:给 key 设的过期时长,到点缓存删除。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL (Time To Live) is the expiry duration set on a key, after which the cache entry is removed.

termDefinitions.term: cache stampede / 缓存击穿(惊群)
termDefinitions.meaning: 热点 key 过期瞬间大量请求同时 miss 打到数据库,可能压垮它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cache stampede is when a hot key expires and many requests miss at once and hit the database, possibly overwhelming it.

termDefinitions.term: request coalescing / 请求合并(single flight)
termDefinitions.meaning: 只让一个请求去重建缓存,其余等它的结果,是最有效的防击穿手段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Request coalescing (single flight) lets only one request rebuild the cache while others wait for its result.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在热点 key 过期前主动刷新;只对 TTL 过期有效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cache warming proactively refreshes hot keys before their TTL elapses; it only helps with TTL-based expiry.

optionExplanations: 对:临近 TTL 就按概率让个别请求提前后台重建,过期前已有人刷新,削平同刻峰。
永不过期会让数据永远陈旧,躲过击穿却牺牲一致性,不是同类手段。
让 key 统一到期只会制造更大的同刻击穿,正好反了。
返回错误把压力甩给客户端,重试后照样一起打库,没解决击穿。
optionExplanations_en: Right: near the TTL a few requests probabilistically rebuild early, so a refresh happens before expiry and flattens the spike.
Never expiring keeps data permanently stale — it dodges stampede but sacrifices consistency, a different tradeoff.
Aligning all keys to one expiry instant only creates a bigger simultaneous stampede — the opposite.
Returning errors pushes load to the client; retries still hit the DB together, so it doesn't solve stampede.

scenario: 团队想上 Write-Through(应用只写缓存、缓存同步落库),手上用的是原生 Redis。
scenario_en: A team wants Write-Through (the app writes only to the cache, which persists to the DB synchronously), using vanilla Redis.
q: 落地这套模式,前提条件是什么?
q_en: What is the prerequisite to implement this pattern?
options: Redis 不原生支持,得靠缓存库插件或应用代码落库
只要在 Redis 配置里打开 write-through 开关就能直接启用
给每个 key 都设好 TTL,过期时缓存会自动写回数据库
改用 Memcached,它能原生把缓存写同步进数据库
options_en: Redis doesn't support it natively; you need a caching library plugin or app code to persist.
Just flip a write-through switch in the Redis config and it's enabled.
Set a TTL on every key and the cache will write back to the DB on expiry.
Switch to Memcached, which natively syncs cache writes into the database.
why: Write-Through 要求缓存在确认写入前先同步落库,而 Redis 没有这个原生能力;必须靠带 data store 插件的缓存库或应用代码实现。代价:引入专用缓存基础设施,也因此面试里不如 cache-aside 常见。
why_en: Write-through must persist to the DB before acknowledging a write, and Redis has no native support for that, so you need a caching library with a data-store plugin or your own application code.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用只写缓存,缓存在确认前先同步落库;读总能拿到新值但写更慢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write-through writes to the cache, which synchronously persists to the DB before acknowledging; reads stay fresh but writes are slower.

termDefinitions.term: data store plugin / 数据存储插件
termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存库里负责调用数据库写逻辑的组件,让缓存能替你落库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A data-store plugin is the component in a caching library that calls your database write logic so the cache can persist for you.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用先查缓存,miss 再查库并回填;面试默认模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cache-aside has the app check the cache first and, on a miss, query the DB and backfill; the default interview pattern.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个内存 key-value 缓存,和 Redis 一样不原生支持写穿。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Memcached is an in-memory key-value cache that, like Redis, does not natively support write-through.

optionExplanations: 对:原生 Redis 缺这能力,得引入专用缓存库或框架来替你落库。
Redis 没有这么个 write-through 开关,原生就不支持这套模式。
TTL 只管过期删除,和「写时同步落库」是两回事,不会自动写回。
Memcached 同样不原生支持写穿,换它也解决不了这个前提。
optionExplanations_en: Right: Redis has no native write-through, so you need a caching library with a data-store plugin or app code to persist.
There is no such write-through switch in Redis; it isn't natively supported.
TTL only handles expiry-delete; it's unrelated to synchronous write-back on write.
Memcached also lacks native write-through, so switching to it doesn't meet the prerequisite.

scenario: 系统写多读少,大量写入的记录之后几乎无人再读。团队用 Write-Through,每次写都同步塞进缓存。
scenario_en: The system is write-heavy and read-light; most written records are rarely read again. The team uses Write-Through, inserting into the cache on every write.
q: 这种搭配会怎样劣化缓存?
q_en: How does this pairing degrade the cache?
options: 写入数据塞满缓存,把真正的热点按 LRU 挤出去
缓存条目因为每次写入而再也无法设置 TTL 过期
每一次写都会清空整个缓存,让命中率瞬间归零
写进去的数据会和数据库对不上,产生脏读
options_en: Written data fills the cache and evicts the actually-hot entries under LRU.
Cache entries can no longer be given a TTL because of each write.
Every write clears the whole cache, dropping the hit rate to zero instantly.
The written data ends up inconsistent with the database, causing dirty reads.
why: 写多读少时,Write-Through 把大量此后无人再读的数据也塞进缓存;它们占着有限内存,按 LRU 把真正的热点条目挤出去,命中率不升反降。这也是为什么它最适合写完马上要读的数据。
why_en: In a write-heavy, read-light workload, write-through fills the cache with entries no one reads again; they occupy scarce memory and evict the actually-hot keys under LRU, so the hit rate drops.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全称 Least Recently Used,最近最少使用:内存满时淘汰最久没被访问的条目。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LRU (Least Recently Used) evicts the entry that has gone the longest without access when memory is full.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用只写缓存,缓存同步落库;每次写都会把数据塞进缓存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write-through writes to the cache, which persists to the DB; every write also inserts data into the cache.

termDefinitions.meaning: 请求在缓存中直接命中的比例;被冷数据挤占后会下降。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hit rate is the fraction of requests served from cache; it drops when cold data crowds out hot entries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全称 Time To Live,存活时间:给 key 设的过期时长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL (Time To Live) is the expiry duration set on a cache key.

optionExplanations: 对:写多读少时缓存被无人再读的数据占满,LRU 把热点挤掉,命中率反降。
写穿不影响 TTL,过期该设还能设,这不是它的污染问题。
写穿是更新对应 key,不会清空整缓存,命中率不会归零。
对不上是双写一致性问题(另一张卡),这里问的是缓存被污染。
optionExplanations_en: Right: write-heavy load fills the cache with never-read data, LRU evicts hot keys, and hit rate falls.
Write-through doesn't block TTLs; you can still set expiry, so this isn't the pollution issue.
Write-through updates the matching key; it doesn't wipe the whole cache or zero the hit rate.
Inconsistency is the dual-write problem (another card); here the issue is cache pollution.

scenario: 「决定缓存什么」定了要缓存用户资料和全站热帖 feed,下一步要想清楚拿什么 key 去查缓存。
scenario_en: After deciding to cache user profiles and the global trending feed, the next step is choosing what key to look them up by.
q: 设计 cache key 最合理的做法是?
q_en: What is the soundest way to design cache keys?
options: 用能唯一定位一条数据的结构化命名 key
每条数据都用随机 UUID 当 key 来避免任何冲突
直接把整条 SQL 查询字符串拿来当缓存 key
全站数据统一挂在同一个全局 key 底下共享
options_en: Use a structured, uniquely-identifying key naming scheme.
Give each record a random UUID key to avoid any collisions.
Just use the full SQL query string as the cache key.
Hang all site data under one shared global key.
why: cache key 是「怎么查」的落点:用结构化命名唯一定位一条数据——用户资料用 user:123:profile,全站热帖用 trending:posts:global。太随机会查不回来,太粗则不同数据互相覆盖。
why_en: The cache key is how you look data up, so name it structurally to identify one record — user:123:profile for a profile, trending:posts:global for the global feed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用来存取一条缓存数据的标识,如 user:123:profile。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cache key is the identifier used to store and look up one cached record, e.g. user:123:profile.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全称 Universally Unique Identifier,全局唯一标识符;随机生成,做缓存 key 会查不回来。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A UUID (Universally Unique Identifier) is a randomly generated unique id; used as a cache key it can't be looked up again.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全称 Structured Query Language,查询关系型数据库的语言;整条语句当 key 太脆。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SQL (Structured Query Language) is the language to query relational databases; a full statement makes a brittle cache key.

optionExplanations: 对:结构化命名能精确定位单条记录,查得回、也不会互相覆盖。
随机 UUID 每次都不同,写进去就再也 lookup 不到,等于没缓存。
整条 SQL 当 key 太脆:空格/参数一变就 miss,还极长难管理。
共用一个全局 key 会让不同数据互相覆盖,只剩最后写入那份。
optionExplanations_en: Right: a structured key like user:123:profile uniquely locates data — retrievable and collision-free.
A random UUID differs every time, so a written value can never be looked up — no caching at all.
A full SQL string is brittle: any whitespace/param change misses, and it's long and hard to manage.
One global key makes different data overwrite each other, leaving only the last write.

scenario: 工程师以为 CDN 只能缓存图片、视频这类静态文件。
scenario_en: An engineer assumes a CDN can only cache static files like images and videos.
q: 关于现代 CDN(Cloudflare/Fastly/Akamai)的能力,正确的是?
q_en: What is true about modern CDNs (Cloudflare/Fastly/Akamai)?
options: 能缓存公开 API 响应、HTML 页,还能在边缘跑逻辑
只能缓存图片、视频这类静态媒体文件,任何动态内容都得一律直接回源站取
能替代 Redis,缓存所有私有用户会话数据
会把动态内容实时同步回写到源站数据库
options_en: They can cache public API responses and HTML pages, and run edge logic.
They can only cache static media files like images and videos; any dynamic content must always go straight to origin.
They can replace Redis and cache all private user session data.
They write dynamic content back to the origin database in real time.
why: 现代 CDN 不止缓存静态媒体:还能缓存公开 API 响应、HTML 页面,并在边缘运行个性化和安全规则。但面试里最稳的引入理由仍是「大规模静态媒体分发」,其余按需展开。
why_en: Modern CDNs cache more than static files — public API responses, HTML pages, and edge logic for personalization and security — but static media at scale is still the safest reason to introduce one in an interview.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全称 Content Delivery Network:把内容缓存在靠近用户的边缘节点;现代 CDN 不止缓存静态文件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN (Content Delivery Network) caches content on edge nodes near users; modern CDNs cache more than static files.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在 CDN 边缘节点运行的小段逻辑,用来做个性化或安全规则。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Edge logic is small code run at CDN edge nodes to personalize content or enforce security rules.

termDefinitions.meaning: CDN 背后的原始服务器,边缘 miss 时回源取内容。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The origin is the source server behind a CDN, fetched from when an edge node misses.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用间调用的接口;现代 CDN 也能缓存公开 API 的响应。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API is an interface for calls between applications; modern CDNs can also cache public API responses.

optionExplanations: 对:它不只静态文件,公开接口响应、网页和边缘逻辑都能缓存或运行。
低估了 CDN:它早已不止静态文件,动态内容也能按规则缓存。
私有会话数据要鉴权、因人而异,不该放公共边缘缓存。
CDN 是读侧缓存,不会把内容实时写回源站数据库。
optionExplanations_en: Right: modern CDNs cache public API responses and HTML, and run personalization/security logic at the edge.
This underrates CDNs: they're long past static-only and can cache dynamic content by rules.
Private session data is auth-gated and per-user; it doesn't belong in a public edge cache.
A CDN is a read-side cache; it doesn't write content back to the origin database in real time.

scenario: Redis 客户端库在本地缓存了集群元数据:哪些节点在集群里、slot 如何分配。
scenario_en: A Redis client library locally caches cluster metadata: which nodes are in the cluster and how slots are assigned.
q: 这层客户端内部缓存买到了什么?
q_en: What does this client-internal cache buy?
options: 客户端能直接路由到正确节点,免去每次问集群
让客户端在断网离线时也能继续读到用户业务数据
替代服务端 Redis,数据不必再存在服务器上
自动把写请求批量、异步地刷进数据库
options_en: The client routes straight to the right node without asking the cluster each time.
The client can keep reading user business data even while offline.
It replaces server-side Redis so data no longer lives on the server.
It automatically flushes writes to the database in async batches.
why: Redis 客户端缓存 cluster metadata——节点列表与 slot 分配,于是每次操作能按 key 算出所在 slot、直连正确节点,省掉先问集群拓扑的往返。这也是客户端缓存的一种,只不过缓存的是拓扑而非业务数据。
why_en: A Redis client caches cluster metadata — the node list and slot assignments — so it can route each operation straight to the right node instead of asking the cluster every time.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis Cluster 把 key 空间划成 16384 个 slot,按 key 决定落在哪个节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A slot is one of the 16384 partitions Redis Cluster splits the keyspace into, deciding which node a key lives on.

termDefinitions.meaning: 集群里有哪些节点、slot 如何分配的拓扑信息;客户端缓存它以直连正确节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cluster metadata is the topology of which nodes exist and how slots are assigned; clients cache it to reach the right node directly.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用只写缓存,缓存异步批量落库;和缓存拓扑元数据无关。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write-behind writes to the cache, which asynchronously batches persistence to the DB; unrelated to caching topology.

optionExplanations: 对:缓存了节点与 slot 分配,客户端能按 key 直连正确节点,免去每次问集群。
离线读业务数据是设备端缓存;这里缓存的是集群拓扑,不是业务数据。
客户端只缓存拓扑元数据,真正的数据仍存在服务端 Redis 上。
批量异步落库是 write-behind,和客户端缓存元数据无关。
optionExplanations_en: Right: caching nodes and slot assignments lets the client reach the right node by key, skipping the cluster lookup.
Offline reads of business data are device caching; here the cache holds cluster topology, not business data.
The client caches only topology metadata; the real data still lives on server-side Redis.
Async batched persistence is write-behind, unrelated to caching cluster metadata.
